newsitem.title: COMOROS: Troops wound three on Comoros island of Anjouan.
newsitem.headline: Troops wound three on Comoros island of Anjouan.

text.p: Troops shot and wounded three stone-throwing secessionists on the Indian Ocean Comoros island of Anjouan on Saturday before taking refuge in a port, witnesses said.
They said clashes between stone-throwing demonstrators and police and troops broke out on Saturday in the Anjouan capital of Mutsamudu and shots were fired when security forces ran out of teargas.
At least three people were shot and wounded, witnesses said.
They said troops under a hail of stones were forced to retreat to the capital's port where an angry mob blocked the gates and set fire to a house owned by Prime Minister Ahmed Abdou.
Police said the prefecture in the town of Sivia west of Mutsamdu was set ablaze on Saturday by a mob of secessionists.
A secessionist leader on Anjouan on Thursday rejected dialogue with the government, saying authorities were insincere.

Comoro Islands Foreign Minister Mountar Ahmed Charif told diplomats in the Comoros capital of Moroni on Thursday the government wanted dialogue with the secessionist movement on Anjouan seeking independence or a return to the French fold.

"No dialogue is possible with the Comoran authorities as long as our president (of the secessionist movement) and our brothers are kept behind bars and we are submitted to ferocious repression," Fatima Mkiri Wa Djimwa told Reuters late on Thursday. She added that the government's appeal was insincere.
Authorities imposed a curfew on Mutsamudu on Monday after clashes between security forces and secessionists in which many were reported wounded.
Secessionists are protesting against the arrest on Monday of their leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, now replaced by Djimwa.

The Comoro Islands have a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue that independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
Three people including a gendarme were killed on Anjouan on July 14 in clashes involving secessionists who tried to raise French flags on Bastille Day. Several people were killed in March.
France has denounced the secessionists. It says the Anjouan situation was serious and could destabilise the whole region.
